symbols.name: Z
symbols.role: stacked assignment matrix with rows in \(\mathcal Z_B\)

symbols.name: \varepsilon_{t,i}
symbols.type: real random variable for \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(i\in\mathcal U\)

symbols.name: Y_{t,i}
symbols.type: real random variable for \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(i\in\mathcal U\)

symbols.name: \mathscr H_t
symbols.def: \(\mathscr H_t\) records assignments, full-vector outcomes, and realized internal randomization through round \(t\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.role: fixed response surfaces, coefficients, and noise kernels

symbols.name: K_{P,t}
symbols.def: \(K_{P,t}(dy_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},z_t)\) is the joint full-outcome kernel supplied by \(P\), with an unrestricted contemporaneous copula.

symbols.name: \Pr_{P,d}
symbols.type: probability law on the complete experimental history
symbols.role: joint law induced only after both an environment and a complete design-decoder pair are fixed

symbols.name: \mathcal T_i(s)
symbols.role: row-coefficient class with an unrestricted direct coordinate

symbols.name: \mathcal D_i
symbols.type: closed convex subset of \(\mathbb R^n\) for each \(i\in\mathcal U\)

symbols.name: v_i
symbols.type: nonnegative real number for each \(i\in\mathcal U\)

symbols.name: \theta_i^{\mathrm D}
symbols.role: unique exact Dantzig target selected by minimum Euclidean norm among the minimum-\(\ell_1\) solutions

symbols.name: r_m
symbols.def: \(r_m=C_{\mathrm{cert}}\sigma\sqrt{(s+1)\log(2n^2/\eta)/(mq)}\), where \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}>0\) is a universal numerical tuning constant.

symbols.name: C_{ij}
symbols.type: three-valued certificate for \(i,j\in\mathcal U\) with \(i\ne j\)

symbols.name: \widehat A
symbols.def: \(\widehat A_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{C_{ij}=\mathsf{edge}\}\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(\widehat A_{ii}=0\) under the directed-support convention.
symbols.role: decoded graph when all certificates decide

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in\mathcal U\) and \(z\in\mathcal Z_B\), \(\mu_i(z)=\alpha_i+z^{\mathsf T}\theta_i\).

For each fixed \(i\in\mathcal U\), every admissible \(d\), every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and every real \(\lambda\), \(\mathbb E_{P,d}[\exp\{\lambda\varepsilon_{t,i}\}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot}]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\).

standard.name: scalar predictable-design conditionally sub-Gaussian martingale innovation

definitions.name: Sparse signed additive-interference class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_s(n,m,B,\delta,\sigma)=\{P:P\text{ satisfies heterogeneous additive network effects, directed row sparsity, beta-min separation, and the rowwise scalar predictable-design conditionally sub-Gaussian martingale-innovation condition for the displayed indices }n,m,B\}\).

definitions.name: Admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder
definitions.construction: \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\), where each \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) is a predictable probability kernel supported on \(\mathcal Z_B\), and \(g\) is \(\mathcal F_m\)-measurable with values in \(\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\); the terminal estimate is \(\widehat A=g(\mathscr H_m)\).

definitions.name: Environment-design probability law
definitions.construction: For an environment \(P\) and an admissible \(d\), \(\Pr_{P,d}\) is the unique sequential law satisfying \(Z_{t\cdot}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\sim\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) and \(Y_{t\cdot}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot}\sim K_{P,t}(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot})\) for every \(t\); it is undefined unless the complete pair \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\) is specified.

definitions.name: Centered exact-budget design
definitions.construction: Given \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) with \(Z_{t\cdot}\in\mathcal Z_B\), set \(H_m=I_m-m^{-1}\mathbf 1_m\mathbf 1_m^{\mathsf T}\) and \(X=H_mZ\).

definitions.name: Sparse-cone curvature
definitions.construction: \(\phi_s(Z)=\min_{i\in\mathcal U}\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U:\,i\in S,\,|S|\le s+1}\inf\{\lVert Xv\rVert_2/(\sqrt m\lVert v\rVert_2):v\ne0,\ \lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le3\lVert v_S\rVert_1\}\).

definitions.name: Random exact-budget pool design
definitions.construction: Under \(\Pi_{m,B}\), the rows \(Z_{t\cdot}\) are independent and uniform on \(\mathcal Z_B\); drawing a row is implemented by a uniformly random permutation of \(\mathcal U\) and treating its first \(B\) entries.

definitions.name: Finite-tolerance row-wise Dantzig decoder
definitions.construction: For each \(i\in\mathcal U\), define \(v_i=\min_{u\in\mathcal D_i}\lVert u\rVert_1\) and \(\theta_i^{\mathrm D}=\arg\min\{\lVert u\rVert_2^2/2:u\in\mathcal D_i,\ \lVert u\rVert_1\le v_i\}\), which is unique. A certified finite-tolerance output \(\widehat\theta_i\) is a feasible point for the latter quadratic program accompanied by a valid dual lower bound whose difference from \(\lVert\widehat\theta_i\rVert_2^2/2\) is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}^2/2\). When \(r_m<\delta/2\), use the explicit coordinate tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}=(\delta-2r_m)/8\). This definition imposes no dimension-only operation or bit-complexity claim for producing the certificate.

definitions.name: Simultaneous edge and nonedge certificates
definitions.construction: For \(i\ne j\), first set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{edge}\) if \(\lvert(\widehat\theta_i)_j\rvert>R_m\); otherwise set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{nonedge}\) if \(\lvert(\widehat\theta_i)_j\rvert<\delta-R_m\), and set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{undecided}\) in the remaining case. Set \(C_{ii}=\mathsf{nonedge}\).

definitions.name: Uniform minimax pool complexity
definitions.construction: \(m^*=\inf\{m:\exists\ d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\text{ that is an admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder, with }\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(g(\mathscr H_m)\ne A)\le\eta\}\).

definitions.name: Constant-row-weight excitation and packing handle
definitions.construction: Optimize a constant-row-weight bipartite incidence design for the weakest structured sparse singular direction, decode all outcome rows with a certificate-producing convex program, and dualize the same excitation program into a signed support packing for the minimax converse.

statements.statement: If \(Z_{t\cdot}\) is uniform on \(\mathcal Z_B\), then \(\operatorname{Cov}(Z_{t\cdot})=p(1-p)\frac{n}{n-1}(I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T})\). Consequently, for every vector \(v\) with \(\lVert v\rVert_0\le k<n\), \(v^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(Z_{t\cdot})v\ge p(1-p)\frac{n-k}{n-1}\lVert v\rVert_2^2\).
statements.justification: This isolates the sole exact-budget null direction and proves that it cannot contain a sufficiently sparse contrast.
statements.gap: Binary compressed-sensing analyses allow other row laws; this lemma gives the exact projector and sparse eigenvalue for complete randomization with fixed treatment count.
statements.consumer: It supplies the population curvature used to design repeated fixed-budget graph-measurement experiments.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(z=Z_{t\cdot}\).  By uniformity on \(\mathcal Z_B\), permutation symmetry gives
\[
 \mathbb E z_j=p,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(z_j)=p(1-p),
 \qquad j\in\mathcal U.
\]
For distinct \(j,k\), the fixed-cardinality constraint and direct counting give
\[
 \mathbb E(z_jz_k)
 =\frac{B(B-1)}{n(n-1)},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(z_j,z_k)
 =\frac{B(B-1)}{n(n-1)}-\frac{B^2}{n^2}
 =-\frac{p(1-p)}{n-1}.
\]
Thus the diagonal and off-diagonal entries of the covariance matrix are respectively \(p(1-p)\) and \(-p(1-p)/(n-1)\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(z)
 =p(1-p)\frac{n}{n-1}
   \left(I_n-\frac1n\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]
Now let \(K=\{j:v_j\ne0\}\), so that \(|K|\le k<n\).  Cauchy--Schwarz on \(K\) yields
\[
 (\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}v)^2
 =\left(\sum_{j\in K}v_j\right)^2
 \le |K|\sum_{j\in K}v_j^2
 \le k\lVert v\rVert_2^2.
\]
Substitution into the covariance formula therefore gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 v^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(z)v
 &=p(1-p)\frac{n}{n-1}
   \left(\lVert v\rVert_2^2-\frac{(\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}v)^2}{n}\right)\\
 &\ge p(1-p)\frac{n-k}{n-1}\lVert v\rVert_2^2,
 \end{aligned}
\]
which proves both assertions.

statements.statement: Fix a legal matrix \(Z\). For every \(i\in\mathcal U\), the noiseless map \((\alpha_i,u)\mapsto\alpha_i\mathbf 1_m+Zu\) is injective on \(\mathbb R\times\mathcal T_i(s)\) if and only if \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\). Hence all signed spillover rows and \(A\) are exactly identified from the full outcome matrix if and only if this single structured sparse singular-value condition holds.
statements.justification: The result gives a necessary-and-sufficient identification boundary rather than treating a restricted eigenvalue as an unexplained sufficient condition.
statements.gap: Wainwright2009 and WangWainwrightRamchandran2010 study support recovery under Gaussian or independently sparsified measurements; neither characterizes the affine exact-budget slice shared by all network rows.
statements.consumer: An experimenter can audit a proposed pool matrix before deployment and know whether any sparse signed graph is observationally aliased.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(F_{i,Z}:\mathbb R\times\mathcal T_i(s)\to\mathbb R^m\) for the observable noiseless row map
\[
F_{i,Z}(a,u)=a\mathbf 1_m+Zu.
\]
We prove the asserted equivalence with the universal quantifier read jointly, namely
\[
\bigl[\text{for every }i\in\mathcal U,\ F_{i,Z}\text{ is injective}\bigr]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \kappa_s(Z)>0. \tag{1}
\]

First suppose \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\), fix \(i\in\mathcal U\), and suppose that
\[
F_{i,Z}(a,u)=F_{i,Z}(a',u')
\qquad
\text{for }(a,u),(a',u')\in\mathbb R\times\mathcal T_i(s).
\]
Set \(b=a-a'\) and \(v=u-u'\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal T_i(s)\),
\[
\operatorname{supp}(v_{-i})
 \subseteq \operatorname{supp}(u_{-i})\cup\operatorname{supp}(u'_{-i}),
\qquad
\lVert v_{-i}\rVert_0\le 2s. \tag{2}
\]
Equality of the two observed vectors gives
\[
b\mathbf 1_m+Zv=0. \tag{3}
\]
Because \(H_m\mathbf 1_m=0\) and \(X=H_mZ\) by the centered-design definition, applying \(H_m\) to (3) yields
\[
Xv=0. \tag{4}
\]
If \(v\ne0\), then (2) makes \(v\) feasible in the infimum defining \(\kappa_s(Z)\), so
\[
0=\frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2}{\sqrt m\lVert v\rVert_2}
 \ge \kappa_s(Z)>0,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus \(v=0\).  Equation (3) then gives \(b\mathbf 1_m=0\), and \(m\ge1\) implies \(b=0\).  Hence \(u=u'\) and \(a=a'\).  Since \(i\) was arbitrary, every \(F_{i,Z}\) is injective.

For the converse, suppose \(\kappa_s(Z)=0\).  We first justify that the zero infimum supplies an exact sparse null vector.  For \(i\in\mathcal U\) and \(J\subseteq\mathcal U\setminus\{i\}\) with \(\lvert J\rvert\le2s\), let
\[
E_{i,J}=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{supp}(v_{-i})\subseteq J\}.
\]
The admissible vectors in the definition of \(\kappa_s(Z)\) form the finite union of the subspaces \(E_{i,J}\).  On each nonempty compact unit sphere
\(E_{i,J}\cap\{v:\lVert v\rVert_2=1\}\), the continuous function \(v\mapsto\lVert Xv\rVert_2/\sqrt m\) attains its minimum.  There are finitely many pairs \((i,J)\).  Consequently the infimum defining \(\kappa_s(Z)\) is attained after normalizing \(v\), and \(\kappa_s(Z)=0\) yields some \(i_0\in\mathcal U\) and \(v\ne0\) such that
\[
\lVert v_{-i_0}\rVert_0\le2s,
\qquad Xv=0. \tag{5}
\]

To obtain not only coefficient aliasing but also graph aliasing, select a row index \(r\) as follows.  If \(v_{-i_0}\ne0\), take \(r=i_0\).  If \(v_{-i_0}=0\), then \(v\) is supported on \(\{i_0\}\); choose any \(r\ne i_0\), which is possible because \(n\ge8\).  In both cases,
\[
1\le\lVert v_{-r}\rVert_0\le2s, \tag{6}
\]
where the upper bound in the second case uses \(s\ge1\).  Partition \(\operatorname{supp}(v_{-r})\) into disjoint sets \(J_0,J_1\) with \(\lvert J_0\rvert\le s\) and \(\lvert J_1\rvert\le s\), which is possible by (6).  Define \(u,u'\in\mathbb R^n\) coordinatewise by
\[
u_r=v_r,
\quad u_j=v_j\ \text{for }j\in J_0,
\quad u_j=0\ \text{otherwise},
\]
and
\[
u'_r=0,
\quad u'_j=-v_j\ \text{for }j\in J_1,
\quad u'_j=0\ \text{otherwise}.
\]
Then
\[
u-u'=v,
\qquad u,u'\in\mathcal T_r(s), \tag{7}
\]
and (6) ensures that the off-diagonal supports of \(u\) and \(u'\) are different.

By (5) and \(X=H_mZ\), \(H_mZv=0\).  Directly from
\(H_m=I_m-m^{-1}\mathbf 1_m\mathbf 1_m^{\mathsf T}\), its kernel is
\(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_m\}\): indeed, \(H_mw=0\) implies
\(w=m^{-1}(\mathbf 1_m^{\mathsf T}w)\mathbf 1_m\).  Therefore there is \(c\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
Zv=c\mathbf 1_m. \tag{8}
\]
Using (7)--(8), we obtain the observational alias
\[
F_{r,Z}(-c,u)-F_{r,Z}(0,u')
=-c\mathbf 1_m+Z(u-u')
=-c\mathbf 1_m+Zv
=0. \tag{9}
\]
The two parameter pairs in (9) are distinct because \(v=u-u'\ne0\).  Hence \(F_{r,Z}\) is not injective, proving the reverse implication in (1).

It remains to connect (1), which concerns an observed-law map, to the causal support target rather than identifying the two by definition.  Under additive interference, the noiseless observed column for outcome row \(i\) is
\[
M_{\cdot i}=\alpha_i\mathbf 1_m+Z\theta_i=F_{i,Z}(\alpha_i,\theta_i). \tag{10}
\]
Directed row sparsity gives \(\theta_i\in\mathcal T_i(s)\), because its off-diagonal support is \(S_i\) and \(\lvert S_i\rvert\le s\).  When \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\), (1) makes the inverse \(F_{i,Z}^{-1}\) single-valued on the range containing \(M_{\cdot i}\).  Thus an explicit noiseless recovery functional is
\[
\widetilde\theta_i(M;Z)
=\operatorname{pr}_2\!\left(F_{i,Z}^{-1}(M_{\cdot i})\right),
\qquad
\mathcal R_Z(M)_{ij}
=\mathbf 1\{j\ne i,\ (\widetilde\theta_i(M;Z))_j\ne0\}. \tag{11}
\]
Equations (10)--(11), rather than a definition of the causal target, prove
\[
\widetilde\theta_i(M;Z)=\theta_i,
\qquad
\mathcal R_Z(M)_{ij}
=\mathbf 1\{i\ne j,\Gamma_{ij}\ne0\}=A_{ij}. \tag{12}
\]
Hence all signed rows and their directed support are exactly identified.

Finally, if \(\kappa_s(Z)=0\), use the two alternatives in (9) as row \(r\) of two additive-interference systems and take identical admissible parameters in every other row.  Both systems satisfy directed row sparsity by (7), and (9) makes their entire noiseless outcome matrices equal.  Nevertheless, their signed row coefficients differ, and their off-diagonal supports differ by (6)--(7), so their matrices \(A\) differ.  No functional of the observed noiseless matrix can therefore recover all signed rows or \(A\) uniformly on the stated model class.  This proves the claimed necessity and completes the identification equivalence.

statements.statement: Assume in addition that \(n\ge9\). There exist universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\), if \(m\ge Cq^{-1}\{(2s+1)\log(en/(2s+1))+\log(2/\rho)\}\), then \(\Pr\{\kappa_s(Z)^2\ge cq,\ \phi_s(Z)^2\ge cq\}\ge1-\rho\). The assignment matrix itself is generated in randomized time polynomial in \(n\) and \(m\).
statements.justification: This turns population excitation into one shared finite pool family that separates every admissible row model and supports stable convex decoding.
statements.gap: AldridgeJohnsonScarlett2016 fixes column weights for Boolean group tests, while LotfiVidyasagar2020 studies binary sensing matrices without the exact row-cardinality and centered-null geometry required here.
statements.consumer: The theorem provides a deployable fixed-budget exploration batch for platforms that observe every unit outcome after each assignment.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply the balanced-pool uniform concentration lemma.  A vector admitted in the definition of \(\kappa_s(Z)\) has at most \(2s+1\) nonzero coordinates, so its first conclusion gives
\[
 \kappa_s(Z)^2\ge c_0q.
\]
Under \(n\ge9\), every vector admitted in the definition of \(\phi_s(Z)\) satisfies the factor-three cone condition in the lemma, and hence
\[
 \phi_s(Z)^2\ge c_0q.
\]
Both inequalities hold on the same event of probability at least \(1-\rho\); renaming the universal constants proves the probability assertion.  By the definition of \(\Pi_{m,B}\), one row is generated by a uniform random permutation of \(\mathcal U\) followed by retaining its first \(B\) entries.  A standard shuffle uses \(O(n)\) elementary randomized operations, so all \(m\) rows are generated in \(O(mn)\) operations.

statements.statement: There are universal choices of \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and \(C>0\) such that, if \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\), \(m\ge Cq^{-1}\{(2s+1)\log(en/(2s+1))+(\sigma^2/\delta^2)(s+1)\log(2n^2/\eta)+\log(2/\rho)\}\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_s\), then the displayed sample-size condition implies \(r_m<\delta/2\). Set \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}=(\delta-2r_m)/8\) and \(R_m=r_m+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\), and for every row take any certified finite-tolerance output in the corrected Dantzig-decoder definition. Its valid primal--dual gap bound and strong convexity give \(\lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i^{\mathrm D}\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\), hence the same coordinatewise bound. With probability at least \(1-\rho-\eta\), simultaneously for every \(i\in\mathcal U\), \(\lVert\theta_i^{\mathrm D}-\theta_i\rVert_\infty\le r_m\) and therefore \(\lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i\rVert_\infty\le R_m\). The numerical margin is \(\delta-2R_m=3(\delta-2r_m)/4>0\), so simultaneously for all \(i\ne j\), \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{edge}\) if \(A_{ij}=1\) and \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{nonedge}\) if \(A_{ij}=0\). Thus \(\widehat A=A\), no certificate is undecided, and every certified finite-tolerance output preserves every inclusion and exclusion certificate. The network-wide probability uses the scalar predictable-design innovation condition for each fixed outcome row at error level \(\eta/n\), followed by a union bound over \(i\in\mathcal U\); no restriction on contemporaneous dependence across outcome rows is imposed. No dimension-only real-arithmetic or bit-complexity bound for finding the certified output is asserted.
statements.justification: This converts rowwise scalar concentration into simultaneous positive and negative graph decisions by an explicit union bound, without assuming cross-unit noise independence; optimization error enters only through a mathematically checkable primal--dual certificate.
statements.gap: ZhangCheng2017 gives simultaneous inference for nonadaptive high-dimensional linear models, and AgarwalAgarwalMasoeroWhitehouse2024 learns unknown interference neighborhoods for regret; neither supplies finite-sample graph-wide inclusion and exclusion certificates under exact-budget pooling.
statements.consumer: YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022 motivates experiments where the network is costly to measure; these certificates determine which directed spillovers can safely enter downstream exposure analysis.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(T_i=\{i\}\cup S_i\).  Directed row sparsity gives \(|T_i|\le s+1\), and additive interference gives
\[
 H_mY_i=X\theta_i+H_m\varepsilon_i,
 \qquad \varepsilon_i=(\varepsilon_{1,i},\ldots,\varepsilon_{m,i})^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Apply the balanced-pool concentration lemma with failure probability \(\rho\).  On its event \(E_Z\), simultaneously for every \(i\),
\[
 \frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m}\ge c_0q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 \lVert v_{T_i^c}\rVert_1\le\lVert v_{T_i}\rVert_1,
 \qquad
 \max_j\lVert Xe_j\rVert_2^2\le2mq.
 \tag{21}
\]
This invokes the factor-one cone conclusion and therefore remains valid at \(n=8,s=1\).

Use the nonadaptive implementation that draws the independent pool rows before observing outcomes.  Conditional on the complete assignment matrix, the weights in each score are deterministic and the rowwise predictable sub-Gaussian bound may be iterated over time.  Since \(X^{\mathsf T}H_m=X^{\mathsf T}\), for fixed \(i,j\),
\[
 \Pr_{P,d}\!\left(
  |e_j^{\mathsf T}X^{\mathsf T}H_m\varepsilon_i|>\lambda_m\mid Z
 \right)
 \le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{\lambda_m^2}
 {2\sigma^2\lVert Xe_j\rVert_2^2}\right)
 \le\frac{\eta}{n^2}.
 \tag{22}
\]
When \(\sigma=0\), the score is zero almost surely and (22) is read by continuity.  A union bound over all \(n^2\) row-coordinate pairs gives an event \(E_\varepsilon\) of conditional probability at least \(1-\eta\) on which
\[
 \max_{i\in\mathcal U}\lVert X^{\mathsf T}H_m\varepsilon_i\rVert_\infty
 \le\lambda_m.
 \tag{23}
\]
Only scalar bounds for fixed outcome rows were used; contemporaneous dependence between different rows is immaterial to the union bound.

On \(E_Z\cap E_\varepsilon\), (20) and (23) imply \(\theta_i\in\mathcal D_i\).  The feasible set is nonempty for every data realization because any least-squares solution satisfies the normal equations, and the minimum defining \(v_i\) is attained by closedness and coercivity of the \(\ell_1\) objective.  Hence \(\theta_i^{\mathrm D}\) is well defined.  Put \(\Delta_i=\theta_i^{\mathrm D}-\theta_i\).  Minimality of its \(\ell_1\) norm and the support of \(\theta_i\) give
\[
 \lVert(\Delta_i)_{T_i^c}\rVert_1
 \le\lVert(\Delta_i)_{T_i}\rVert_1.
 \tag{24}
\]
Feasibility of both vectors gives
\[
 \lVert X^{\mathsf T}X\Delta_i\rVert_\infty\le2\lambda_m.
 \tag{25}
\]
Using (21), (24), Cauchy--Schwarz, and (25), in that order,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c_0mq\lVert\Delta_i\rVert_2^2
 &\le\lVert X\Delta_i\rVert_2^2
 =\Delta_i^{\mathsf T}X^{\mathsf T}X\Delta_i\\
 &\le2\lambda_m\lVert\Delta_i\rVert_1
 \le4\lambda_m\sqrt{s+1}\lVert\Delta_i\rVert_2.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{26}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \lVert\theta_i^{\mathrm D}-\theta_i\rVert_\infty
 \le C_7\sigma\sqrt{\frac{(s+1)\log(2n^2/\eta)}{mq}}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Choose \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge C_7\).  The noise-to-signal term in the sample-size hypothesis then implies
\[
 r_m^2=C_{\mathrm{cert}}^2\sigma^2
 \frac{(s+1)\log(2n^2/\eta)}{mq}<\frac{\delta^2}{4},
 \tag{28}
\]
after one universal enlargement of \(C\).

For a certified feasible \(\widehat\theta_i\), weak duality bounds its objective excess over the unique minimizer by \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}^2/2\).  The variational inequality at the constrained minimizer and one-strong convexity of \(u\mapsto\lVert u\rVert_2^2/2\) imply
\[
 \frac12\lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i^{\mathrm D}\rVert_2^2
 \le\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}^2}{2}.
 \tag{29}
\]
Thus its Euclidean and coordinatewise errors are at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\).  Combining (27)--(29),
\[
 \lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i\rVert_\infty\le R_m,
 \qquad
 \delta-2R_m=\frac34(\delta-2r_m)>0.
 \tag{30}
\]
If \(A_{ij}=0\), then \(|(\widehat\theta_i)_j|\le R_m<\delta-R_m\), so the certificate is \(\mathsf{nonedge}\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), beta-min and (30) give
\[
 |(\widehat\theta_i)_j|\ge|\Gamma_{ij}|-R_m
 \ge\delta-R_m>R_m,
\]
so it is \(\mathsf{edge}\).  Therefore no certificate is undecided and \(\widehat A=A\).  Finally, \(\Pr(E_Z\cap E_\varepsilon)\ge1-\rho-\eta\), proving the proposed statement.  The proof uses only the validity of the supplied optimization certificate and deliberately makes no complexity claim for finding it.

statements.statement: When \(B=1\) and \(Z\) consists of \(r\) repetitions of every singleton assignment, \(m=nr\) and \(m^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X=n^{-1}(I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T})\). Thus \(\kappa_s(Z)^2\ge n^{-1}(1-(2s+1)/n)\), recovering the classical one-unit-at-a-time identification benchmark.
statements.justification: The reduction checks the fixed-budget geometry at its most restrictive boundary.
statements.gap: The proposition is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim; it exposes how the general criterion collapses to repeated coordinate measurements.
statements.consumer: It gives a transparent baseline against which pooled designs can be compared in small-budget experiments.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(e_j\in\{0,1\}^n\) denote the \(j\)-th coordinate vector.  By the hypothesis on \(Z\), each \(e_j\), \(j\in\mathcal U\), occurs as a row of \(Z\) exactly \(r\) times.  Every such row belongs to \(\mathcal Z_1\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\mbox{-}budget\mbox{-}actions}\), and counting the rows gives
\[
m=\sum_{j=1}^n r=nr.
\]
The same repetition property yields
\[
Z^{\mathsf T}Z=\sum_{j=1}^n r e_je_j^{\mathsf T}=rI_n,
\qquad
Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_m=\sum_{j=1}^n r e_j=r\mathbf 1_n.
\]
By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}centered\mbox{-}design}\), \(X=H_mZ\), where \(H_m\) is symmetric and idempotent.  Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
X^{\mathsf T}X
&=Z^{\mathsf T}H_m^{\mathsf T}H_mZ
=Z^{\mathsf T}H_mZ\\
&=Z^{\mathsf T}Z-\frac{1}{m}Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_m\mathbf 1_m^{\mathsf T}Z\\
&=rI_n-\frac{r^2}{nr}\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}
=r\left(I_n-\frac{1}{n}\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Dividing by \(m=nr\) proves
\[
\frac{1}{m}X^{\mathsf T}X
=\frac{1}{n}\left(I_n-\frac{1}{n}\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]

It remains to verify the structured sparse singular-value bound.  Fix \(i\in\mathcal U\) and a nonzero \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert v_{-i}\rVert_0\le 2s\), as in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}structured\mbox{-}singular\mbox{-}value}\).  With \(K=\{j:v_j\ne0\}\), this restriction implies \(\lvert K\rvert\le 2s+1\).  Because \(v\ne0\), the set \(K\) is nonempty, and the elementary sum-of-squares identity
\[
\lvert K\rvert\sum_{j\in K}v_j^2-\left(\sum_{j\in K}v_j\right)^2
=\sum_{\substack{j,\ell\in K\\j<\ell}}(v_j-v_\ell)^2
\ge0
\]
shows that \(\left(\sum_{j\in K}v_j\right)^2\le\lvert K\rvert\sum_{j\in K}v_j^2\).  Hence the displayed Gram identity gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m\lVert v\rVert_2^2}
&=\frac{1}{n}\left(1-\frac{(\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}v)^2}{n\lVert v\rVert_2^2}\right)\\
&=\frac{1}{n}\left(1-\frac{\left(\sum_{j\in K}v_j\right)^2}{n\sum_{j\in K}v_j^2}\right)\\
&\ge \frac{1}{n}\left(1-\frac{\lvert K\rvert}{n}\right)\\
&\ge \frac{1}{n}\left(1-\frac{2s+1}{n}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominators are nonzero because \(n\ge8\) and \(v\ne0\).  Moreover, the stipulated range \(s\le\lfloor n/8\rfloor\) implies \(2s+1<n\), so the final lower bound is positive.  Since the inequality holds for every admissible \(i\) and \(v\), taking first the infimum over \(v\) and then the minimum over \(i\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}structured\mbox{-}singular\mbox{-}value}\), and using nonnegativity of the norm ratio, yields
\[
\kappa_s(Z)^2\ge \frac{1}{n}\left(1-\frac{2s+1}{n}\right).
\]
Thus repeated singleton assignments have precisely the stated centered coordinate-design geometry and its associated one-unit-at-a-time identification bound.

statements.statement: There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, on the Gaussian-noise subclass of \(\mathcal M_s\), every admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\) satisfying \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(g(\mathscr H_m)\ne A)\le\eta\) obeys \(m\ge c\,\sigma^2(\log(n-1)+\log(1/\eta))/(q\delta^2)\). In the noiseless degree-one subclass, every admissible \(d\) that identifies \(A\) uniformly also obeys \(m\ge\max\{\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil,\lceil1/q\rceil\}\).
statements.justification: The converse prices the least-observed treatment side even when assignments react to all past outcome vectors.
statements.gap: WangWainwrightRamchandran2010 proves information limits for independently sparsified random measurements; the stated lower bound instead ranges over adaptive, constant-row-weight causal experiments with unknown baselines.
statements.consumer: The bound tells an experimentation platform when no adaptive scheduling rule can certify the graph within its available number of rounds.

statements.statement:
There are universal constants \(c_0,C_0>0\) with the following property.  Let \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\).  If
\[
 m\ge C_0q^{-1}\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)+\log\!\left(\frac2\rho\right)\right\},
\]
then, with probability at least \(1-\rho\), all three conclusions below hold:
\[
 \frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m}\ge c_0q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 \lVert v\rVert_0\le2s+1,
\]
\[
 \frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m}\ge c_0q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{whenever there is }S\subseteq\mathcal U, |S|\le s+1,
 \text{ with }\lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le\lVert v_S\rVert_1,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\mathcal U}\lVert Xe_j\rVert_2^2\le2mq.
\]
If \(n\ge9\), the second conclusion also holds, after decreasing \(c_0\) universally, under the larger cone condition \(\lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le3\lVert v_S\rVert_1\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(h=\min\{B,n-B\}=nq\).  For one row, put \(\xi=Z_{t\cdot}-p\mathbf 1_n\).  If \(B\le n/2\), then
\[
 \xi^{\mathsf T}u=\sum_{j\in R}(u_j-\bar u),
 \qquad \bar u=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n u_j,
 \tag{1}
\]
where \(R\) is a uniform \(h\)-subset.  If \(B>n/2\), the same identity holds with a minus sign and \(R\) the untreated \(h\)-subset.  Thus it is enough to analyze the right side of (1).

We first repair the moment calculation by an exchangeable-pair recursion.  Let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(\sum_j a_j=0\), let \(W=\sum_{j\in R}a_j\), choose \(I\) uniformly from \(R\) and \(J\) uniformly from \(R^c\), and put
\[
 R'=(R\setminus\{I\})\cup\{J\},
 \qquad W'=W-a_I+a_J,
 \qquad \lambda_0=\frac{n}{h(n-h)}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The pair \((W,W')\) is exchangeable, and direct conditional averaging gives
\[
 \mathbb E(W'-W\mid R)
 =-\left(\frac1h+\frac1{n-h}\right)W
 =-\lambda_0W.
 \tag{3}
\]
For every integer \(\ell\ge1\), exchangeability and (3) imply the exact identity
\[
 \mathbb EW^{2\ell}
 =\frac1{2\lambda_0}\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[(W'-W)
       (W'^{\,2\ell-1}-W^{2\ell-1})\right].
 \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, exchangeability changes the sign of
\((W'-W)\{W'^{\,2\ell-1}+W^{2\ell-1}\}\), so its expectation is zero, while conditioning
\((W'-W)W^{2\ell-1}\) on \(R\) gives
\(-\lambda_0\mathbb EW^{2\ell}\).

The conditional squared increment has the deterministic bound
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[(W'-W)^2\mid R\right]
 &\le
 2h^{-1}\sum_{i\in R}a_i^2+
 2(n-h)^{-1}\sum_{j\notin R}a_j^2\\
 &\le2\lambda_0\lVert a\rVert_2^2.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{5}
\]
Using
\[
 |(x-y)(x^{2\ell-1}-y^{2\ell-1})|
 \le(2\ell-1)(x-y)^2
       (|x|^{2\ell-2}+|y|^{2\ell-2})
\]
in (4), then exchangeability and (5), yields the recursion
\[
 \mathbb E|W|^{2\ell}
 \le2(2\ell-1)\lVert a\rVert_2^2
       \mathbb E|W|^{2\ell-2}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The exact covariance of simple random sampling gives
\[
 \mathbb EW^2
 =\frac{h(n-h)}{n(n-1)}\lVert a\rVert_2^2
 \le2q\lVert a\rVert_2^2.
\]
Iteration of (6), and Cauchy--Schwarz between the two adjacent even moments for odd orders, therefore prove, for every integer \(r\ge2\),
\[
 \mathbb E|W|^r
 \le q(C_1r)^{r/2}\lVert a\rVert_2^r.
 \tag{7}
\]
Thus the relevant \(2\ell\)-th moment is \(q(C\ell)^\ell\), not the invalid
\((2\ell)!\) bound left after exponential-series division.

Since \(a=u-\bar u\mathbf 1_n\) satisfies \(\lVert a\rVert_2\le\lVert u\rVert_2\), (7) implies the Bernstein moment condition.  More explicitly, with \(V=W^2-\mathbb EW^2\), there are numerical \(v_0,c_0'>0\) such that, for every \(\ell\ge2\),
\[
 \mathbb E|V|^\ell
 \le \frac{\ell!}{2}(v_0q\lVert u\rVert_2^4)
       (c_0'\lVert u\rVert_2^2)^{\ell-2}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The same bound (7), applied to both signs of the exponential parameter and using \(\mathbb EW=0\), gives the analogous Bernstein moment-generating-function bound for \(W\), with variance proxy \(Cq\lVert u\rVert_2^2\) and scale \(C\lVert u\rVert_2\).  Independence of the rows under \(\Pi_{m,B}\), the exponential Markov inequality, and (8) therefore yield, for every \(x>0\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{
  \left|\frac1m\sum_{t=1}^m(\xi_t^{\mathsf T}u)^2
        -\mathbb E(\xi^{\mathsf T}u)^2\right|
  >C_2\lVert u\rVert_2^2
       \left(\sqrt{\frac{qx}{m}}+\frac{x}{m}\right)
 \right\}\le2e^{-x},
 \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{
  |\bar\xi^{\mathsf T}u|>
  C_2\lVert u\rVert_2
       \left(\sqrt{\frac{qx}{m}}+\frac{x}{m}\right)
 \right\}\le2e^{-x},
 \qquad \bar\xi=m^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^m\xi_t.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus (9), unlike the discarded argument, follows from a genuine Bernstein moment bound for the quadratic variable.

Let
\[
 M=m^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^m\xi_t\xi_t^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \Sigma=\mathbb E(\xi\xi^{\mathsf T}).
\]
For each support of size at most \(r\), choose a \(1/4\)-net of its Euclidean unit sphere with at most \(9^r\) points.  Padding smaller supports to size \(r\) shows that the number of choices is at most \((en/r)^r\).  Applying (9)--(10) to all net points and using
\[
 \lVert D\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\max_{u\ \text{ in the net}}|u^{\mathsf T}Du|,
 \qquad
 \lVert b\rVert_2
 \le2\max_{u\ \text{ in the net}}|b^{\mathsf T}u|
 \tag{11}
\]
on each support gives, with probability at least \(1-4e^{-x}\),
\[
 d_r:=\sup_{\substack{\lVert u\rVert_2=1\\\lVert u\rVert_0\le r}}
 |u^{\mathsf T}(M-\Sigma)u|
 \le C_3\left(\sqrt{\frac{qL_r}{m}}+\frac{L_r}{m}\right),
 \tag{12}
\]
\[
 b_r:=\sup_{\substack{\lVert u\rVert_2=1\\\lVert u\rVert_0\le r}}
 |\bar\xi^{\mathsf T}u|
 \le C_3\left(\sqrt{\frac{qL_r}{m}}+\frac{L_r}{m}\right),
 \qquad L_r=r\log(en/r)+x.
 \tag{13}
\]

We shall also use the following deterministic consequence of (12)--(13).  If \(D\) is symmetric, decreasing rearrangement of the coordinates of \(v\) into blocks of size \(\lfloor r/2\rfloor\), followed by polarization on every pair of blocks, gives
\[
 |v^{\mathsf T}Dv|
 \le C_4d_r\left(\lVert v\rVert_2+\frac{\lVert v\rVert_1}{\sqrt r}\right)^2.
 \tag{14}
\]
The same blocking without polarization gives
\[
 |b^{\mathsf T}v|
 \le C_4b_r\left(\lVert v\rVert_2+\frac{\lVert v\rVert_1}{\sqrt r}\right).
 \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, monotone ordering bounds the sum of the Euclidean norms of all blocks after the first by \(2\lVert v\rVert_1/\sqrt r\); summing the resulting within-block and cross-block products proves (14)--(15).

Take \(r=\min\{n,\lceil C_5(s+1)\rceil\}\), with \(C_5\) a sufficiently large numerical constant, and set \(x=\log(4/\rho)\).  Since \(s\le n/8\),
\[
 L_r\le C_6\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)
                       +\log\!\left(\frac2\rho\right)\right\}.
 \tag{16}
\]
The assumed lower bound on \(m\) makes the right sides of (12)--(13), respectively, at most an arbitrarily small universal multiple of \(q\) and of \(\sqrt q\).

It remains to compare with the population.  By the exact-budget covariance lemma,
\[
 \Sigma=p(1-p)\frac{n}{n-1}
 \left(I_n-\frac1n\mathbf 1_n\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}\right).
 \tag{17}
\]
Because \(p(1-p)=q(1-q)\ge q/2\), the sparse consequence of that lemma and \(2s+1<n\) give
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v\ge c_1q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{if }\lVert v\rVert_0\le2s+1.
 \tag{18}
\]
For a cone vector, write \(k=|S|\), \(N=n-k\), \(u=\lVert v_S\rVert_1\), and \(w=\lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\).  If \(w\le a_0u\) and \(N>a_0k\), Cauchy--Schwarz separately on the two blocks and maximization over \(0\le w/u\le a_0\) give
\[
 \frac{(\mathbf 1_n^{\mathsf T}v)^2}{n\lVert v\rVert_2^2}
 \le \frac{(1+a_0)^2kN}{n(N+a_0^2k)}.
 \tag{19}
\]
For \(a_0=1\), \(k\le s+1\) and \(s\le n/8\) make (19) at most \(3/4\), including \(n=8,s=1\).  Hence (17) gives
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v\ge(q/8)\lVert v\rVert_2^2.
 \tag{20}
\]
For \(a_0=3\), the additional condition \(n\ge9\) gives \(k/n\le2/9\) and \(N>3k\); the right side of (19) is then at most \(224/225\).  Thus
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}\Sigma v\ge(q/450)\lVert v\rVert_2^2.
 \tag{21}
\]
The respective cone conditions also give \(\lVert v\rVert_1\le(1+a_0)\sqrt{s+1}\lVert v\rVert_2\).  Equations (12)--(16), with their universal constants chosen small relative to (18), (20), and (21), therefore transfer all three population lower bounds to the sample matrix because
\[
 \frac1mX^{\mathsf T}X=M-\bar\xi\bar\xi^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{22}
\]
Finally, \(e_j^{\mathsf T}\Sigma e_j=p(1-p)\le q\).  Equation (12) for one-sparse vectors and (22) imply
\[
 m^{-1}\lVert Xe_j\rVert_2^2\le2q
\]
simultaneously for all \(j\), after a final universal enlargement of \(C_0\).  This proves every asserted conclusion.

statements.statement: For every exact-budget assignment matrix \(Z\), \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\) implies \(m\ge2s+2\).
statements.proof_tex:
Since \(H_m\) is an orthogonal projector of rank \(m-1\), the centered design satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(X)=\operatorname{rank}(H_mZ)\le m-1.
\]
Suppose toward a contradiction that \(m\le2s+1\).  Fix \(i\in\mathcal U\) and choose a coordinate set \(T\subseteq\mathcal U\) of size \(m\) containing \(i\); this is possible because \(m\le2s+1<n\).  The \(m\)-column matrix \(X_T\) has rank at most \(m-1\), so there is a nonzero vector \(v\) supported on \(T\) with \(Xv=0\).  Moreover \(\lVert v_{-i}\rVert_0\le m-1\le2s\).  This vector is feasible in the infimum defining \(\kappa_s(Z)\), and it makes that infimum zero, contradicting \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\).  Hence \(m\ge2s+2\).

statements.statement:
Define
\[
 U_{\mathrm D}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{4n^2}{\eta}\right)
 +\log\!\left(\frac4\eta\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 U_{\mathrm L}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{8n^3}{\eta}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}\log\!\left(\frac{8n^2}{\eta}\right)\right\},
\]
where \(C>0\) is universal.  Then the presently proved nonasymptotic answer to the sharp-pool-complexity question is the two-sided bracket
\[
 c\,\frac{\sigma^2\{\log(n-1)+\log(1/\eta)\}}{q\delta^2}
 \le m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)
 \le \left\lceil\min\{U_{\mathrm D},U_{\mathrm L}\}\right\rceil.
\]
The \(U_{\mathrm D}\) witness is the simultaneous Dantzig certificate with a mathematically valid finite-tolerance optimization certificate; the \(U_{\mathrm L}\) witness is exact rowwise partially penalized Lasso.  Thus the factor \(s+1\) in the Dantzig noise-to-signal term is not intrinsic to exact convex support recovery, but the proved Lasso alternative pays \((s+1)\log(8n^3/\eta)\) for simultaneous empirical strict dual feasibility.  No dimension-only finite-precision complexity guarantee is proved for either optimization output.  Separately, probability-one identification on the noiseless degree-one subclass requires
\[
 m\ge\max\{\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil,\lceil1/q\rceil\},
\]
and every fixed design with \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\) requires \(m\ge2s+2\).  The gap between the displayed lower bound and the better of the two upper bounds remains unresolved outside regimes in which their orders coincide.
statements.justification: The theorem gives two explicit observable-design upper maps and the valid adaptive information lower map, while stating exactly which sparse exploration and computational gaps remain.
statements.gap: The Dantzig and partially penalized Lasso witnesses trade the sparse exploration term against the noise term; the current adaptive converse does not match both in every regime.
statements.consumer: The bracket lets a platform choose the shorter certified pilot for its sparsity and signal-to-noise regime without treating an unproved universal sharp rate as established.

statements.statement:
There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, if
\[
 m\ge Cq^{-1}\left\{(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{8n^3}{\eta}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}\log\!\left(\frac{8n^2}{\eta}\right)\right\},
\]
then independent uniform exact-budget pools together with the rowwise partially penalized Lasso, leaving coordinate \(i\) unpenalized and using a sufficiently small universal penalty \(c_{\mathrm L}q\delta\), define an admissible exact decoder satisfying
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(\widehat A\ne A)\le\eta.
\]
The decoder uses the minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer off the unique-solution event and declares \(A_{ij}=1\) exactly when the penalized coordinate \(j\ne i\) of the selected minimizer is nonzero.  This is a statistical exact-minimizer statement and makes no finite-precision operation or bit-complexity claim.

Determine \(m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)\) up to universal constants in every regime, and construct a polynomial-real-arithmetic-time exact-budget design-decoder pair whose simultaneous edge and nonedge certificates attain that value. In particular, decide whether the factor \(s+1\) multiplying the noise-to-signal term in the simultaneous-certificate theorem is intrinsic to polynomial-time uniform certification or can be removed while preserving the exact-budget constraint.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved content: the upper and lower bounds isolate a computational-statistical gap rather than declaring an unverified sharp rate.
statements.gap: No located paper resolves the joint dependence on treatment fraction, row sparsity, beta-min, and network-wide confidence for signed exact-cardinality measurements.
statements.consumer: A sharp answer determines the shortest pilot experiment needed before using a learned graph in Instagram-style interference characterization or marketplace cluster design.

sampling_model.design: Each row of \(Z\) is a legal assignment in \(\mathcal Z_B\); the attaining construction draws independent uniform rows, while the converse ranges over complete pairs \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\) with predictable exact-budget kernels and an \(\mathcal F_m\)-measurable decoder.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units and all potential-outcome coefficients are fixed; all \(n\) outcomes are observed after each of the \(m\) assignments.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with exactly \(B\) treated units in every round.
sampling_model.overlap: The relevant excitation scale is \(q=\min\{B/n,1-B/n\}\); no independent-coordinate overlap assumption is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Unit baselines are eliminated by \(H_m\); direct effects and sparse spillover rows are estimated jointly by the row-wise Dantzig programs. The computed coefficients have certified coordinate tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}=(\delta-2r_m)/8\) when \(r_m<\delta/2\). Scalar innovation concentration is applied separately to each outcome row at error level \(\eta/n\), and a union bound supplies the network-wide guarantee; contemporaneous innovations may be arbitrarily dependent across units.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under heterogeneous additive network effects and historical baseline information, a completely randomized design yields an unbiased low-variance total-effect estimator without knowledge of the network.
For noisy linear observations with standard Gaussian measurement vectors, necessary and sufficient conditions characterize asymptotically perfect support recovery by an optimal decoder.
Necessary support-recovery conditions for independently sparsified measurement ensembles reveal regimes in which measurement sparsity changes statistical efficiency.
Constant-column-weight nonadaptive Boolean group-testing designs improve the achievable rate of the COMP decoder over Bernoulli testing designs.
Sparse linear representations and regression-based algorithms attain low regret with both known and unknown unit-specific interference neighborhoods.
A bootstrap-assisted de-sparsified-Lasso procedure provides simultaneous inference in nonadaptive high-dimensional sparse linear models.

Under passive CSMA/CA traffic snapshots, direct-graph recovery has matching order-\(d^2\log n\) upper and lower observation laws, while directed hidden-edge recovery from binary ACK/NACK feedback has matching laws depending on direct degree, hidden degree, traffic probability, and minimum collision probability.

tldr: Repeated exact-budget assignments turn unknown additive interference into \(n\) sparse regressions sharing a single highly constrained design. The proposal characterizes noiseless identification by a structured sparse singular value, proves that uniform fixed-cardinality pools excite every legal row contrast, and builds simultaneous edge and nonedge certificates with an explicit polynomial-real-arithmetic optimization margin under beta-min and sub-Gaussian noise. A converse prices the least-observed treatment side over predictable assignment kernels and terminal-history-measurable decoders. The remaining open question is the sharp minimax pool count and whether polynomial-time certification must pay the upper bound's extra sparsity factor.

project_justification.gap: Unknown-network causal papers either bypass graph recovery or learn neighborhoods while optimizing regret, passive wireless graph-recovery papers observe CSMA/CA activations and ACK/NACK events, and sparse-recovery papers use Gaussian, independently sparsified, or Boolean observation schemes; none obeys a designed treatment-total constraint with signed full-vector responses.
project_justification.niche: Full-vector network experiments reuse each exact-cardinality assignment across all outcome rows, creating an affine all-ones null direction but also allowing all directed neighborhoods to be decoded in parallel.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an exact injectivity criterion, a constant-row-weight restricted-excitation theorem, a polynomial-real-arithmetic certificate-producing decoder with an explicit numerical buffer, and adaptive information lower bounds over fully measurable design-decoder pairs on the same directed signed model.

related_work: YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022 establishes the heterogeneous additive network-effects model and shows how total effects can sometimes be estimated without measuring the graph; the present target is the graph itself. AgarwalAgarwalMasoeroWhitehouse2024 uses sparse unit-specific neighborhoods to obtain low regret with an unknown network but does not require uniform signed support decisions under exact-cardinality assignments. GleichLaberVolfovsky2026 couples graph learning and policy choice and motivates repeated full-outcome experimentation, but its discovery results do not characterize the constant-row-weight sparse-identification boundary. YangDraperNowak2016 proves upper and minimax lower observation laws for recovering direct and directed hidden wireless-interference graphs from passive CSMA/CA traffic snapshots; its activation vector is generated by random traffic and carrier-sense backoff, while its hidden-edge response is the binary ACK/NACK success indicator observed only for transmitting access points. Those passive observations cannot simulate the present experiment because they neither let the investigator choose an exact-\(B\) activation vector nor reveal signed additive response magnitudes for every unit after each assignment. Wainwright2009 and WangWainwrightRamchandran2010 provide the information-theoretic support-recovery templates for Gaussian and independently sparsified designs. AldridgeJohnsonScarlett2016 studies constant-column-weight Boolean group tests, whose observation operator and budget orientation differ from signed additive full-vector responses. LotfiVidyasagar2020 supplies robust-null-space tools for binary sensing matrices without requiring every experimental row to contain exactly \(B\) ones. ZhangCheng2017 motivates network-wide simultaneous decisions but treats a nonadaptive high-dimensional regression rather than one constrained design shared across causal outcome rows.
honest_scope: The exact injectivity theorem, random-pool excitation theorem, certificate upper bound, and adaptive lower bound are all proof obligations. The finite-sample upper bound retains a factor \(s+1\) in the noise term; closing or proving necessary that factor is the open-ended question. The computational guarantee is polynomial in real-arithmetic operations with oracle access to observed reals and logarithmic dependence on the explicit coordinate tolerance; it is not a bit-complexity claim for unencoded real outcomes. The simultaneous certificate claim uses only rowwise scalar martingale-innovation control and permits arbitrary contemporaneous dependence across units. The proposal identifies a directed additive support; it does not cover nonlinear exposure mappings, latent outcomes, or misspecified additivity. The \(B=1\) reduction must reproduce repeated singleton measurement exactly.
